sizing_routine.expression: sum(p.stat().st_size for p in root.rglob('*') if p.is_file())
sizing_routine.note: pathlib's rglob('*') matches dot-prefixed names, so .runtime files and .writer.lock are inside the routine’s domain; demonstrated below with a sentinel

retained_native_collection.observation: retained native .runtime holds 0 regular files across 3 directories (crawl4ai cache tree created empty); a zero-byte .writer.lock exists. Valid observation of this run; NOT evidence of nonzero runtime overhead, so the sentinel-clone demonstration below is used per LEAD-03.

du_note_correction.earlier_o2_note: c2 o2_note claimed "du -sb exceeds the per-file sum", while the recorded numbers were equal
du_note_correction.correction: du -sb implies --apparent-size, so it reports per-file apparent bytes PLUS directory-entry apparent sizes; on this filesystem the directory entries reported 0/negligible apparent size for these small trees, so du -sb equaled the per-file sum. The product routine sums regular-file apparent sizes only (no directories), which is what the byte allowance bounds. Filesystem BLOCK usage (du without --apparent-size) is larger and is NOT what the product measures. No exact persisted-byte ceiling is claimed.

export_note: only this measurement report is exported; .runtime trees and the clone are not exported
